findings.title: Mini Shai-Hulud npm Worm Resurges — 169 Compromised Packages incl. TanStack + UiPath, Trusted-Publisher Workflow Propagation
findings.affected_technology: npm ecosystem (TanStack family, UiPath packages, 160+ additional; multi-ecosystem worm — npm/PyPI/Composer/RubyGems/Go demonstrated in prior waves)
findings.summary: Mini Shai-Hulud second wave compromised 169 npm packages including TanStack and UiPath, harvesting CI/CD secrets and self-propagating through trusted-publisher workflows — escalation of the April 29 campaign.
findings.first_seen_at: aikido.dev — Mini Shai-Hulud Is Back: npm Worm Hits over 160 Packages

findings.title: CVE-2026-42208 LiteLLM Pre-Auth SQL Injection — Added to CISA KEV (Active Exploitation Now Federally Mandated)
findings.affected_technology: BerriAI LiteLLM proxy < 1.83.7 (self-hosted AI provider broker)
findings.summary: CISA added LiteLLM's pre-auth SQL injection (covered 2026-04-29) to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-05-11, formalising over two weeks of in-the-wild exploitation with a federal 21-day patch deadline.
findings.first_seen_at: securityaffairs.com — CISA adds BerriAI LiteLLM flaw to KEV catalog

findings.title: Checkmarx Jenkins AST Plugin Compromise (TeamPCP) — Credential-Stealing Plugin Live on Jenkins Marketplace
findings.affected_technology: Checkmarx Jenkins AST plugin (malicious version 2026.5.09; safe baseline 2.0.13-829.vc72453fa_1c16) on Jenkins Marketplace
findings.summary: TeamPCP published a malicious 2026.5.09 build of the Checkmarx Jenkins AST plugin to the Jenkins Marketplace on 2026-05-09 after maintaining ~30 days of GitHub access via stolen Trivy-breach credentials Checkmarx never rotated.
findings.first_seen_at: bleepingcomputer.com — Official CheckMarx Jenkins package compromised with infostealer

findings.title: Google GTIG — First Documented Use of AI-Generated Zero-Day Exploit in the Wild (2FA Bypass Against Open-Source Web Admin Tool)
findings.affected_technology: Unnamed open-source Python-based web administration tool (vendor notified, name withheld pending patch)
findings.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group disclosed the first observed case of threat actors weaponising an AI-generated zero-day exploit in the wild — a 2FA bypass logic-bug against an unnamed open-source Python web admin tool, foiled before mass exploitation.
findings.first_seen_at: bleepingcomputer.com — Google: Hackers used AI to develop zero-day exploit for web admin tool

findings.title: CVE-2026-43284 / CVE-2026-43500 Dirty Frag — Microsoft Defender Confirms In-the-Wild Exploitation; Attack Chain Includes GLPI LDAP Tampering
findings.affected_technology: Linux kernel (xfrm-ESP IPsec page-cache write + RxRPC/RxKAD page-cache write)
findings.summary: Microsoft Defender confirmed limited in-the-wild exploitation of the Dirty Frag Linux kernel LPE chain with a documented attack flow that tampers GLPI LDAP authentication files and PHP session contents after gaining root.
findings.first_seen_at: securityweek.com — New Dirty Frag Linux Vulnerability Possibly Exploited in Attacks

findings.title: GitHub Copilot CLI CVE-2026-45033 — Nested Bare Repository to Arbitrary Command Execution (Fifth AI-Agent Attack Surface in 12 Days)
findings.summary: GitHub Copilot CLI honours a nested bare repository's core.fsmonitor configuration when invoked in an outer working tree, allowing arbitrary command execution as the developer simply by cloning a crafted repository.

findings.title: Next.js Multi-CVE Batch (6 CVEs) — Middleware/Proxy Bypass x4, SSRF, DoS
findings.affected_technology: Next.js (next npm) — Pages Router with i18n, App Router segment-prefetch, Cache Components, dynamic route parameter routing
findings.summary: Next.js shipped a coordinated 6-CVE batch on 2026-05-11 covering four middleware/proxy bypass paths (including an incomplete-fix follow-up on segment-prefetch), a Cache Components WebSocket-upgrade SSRF, and a connection-exhaustion DoS.
findings.first_seen_at: github.com/advisories — GHSA-36qx-fr4f-26g5 / GHSA-492v-c6pp-mqqv / GHSA-267c-6grr-h53f / GHSA-26hh-7cqf-hhc6 / GHSA-c4j6-fc7j-m34r / GHSA-mg66-mrh9-m8jx

findings.title: VulnCheck OpenClaw 16-CVE Batch (CVE-2026-44991 to CVE-2026-45006) — Second Mass-Disclosure Wave in 72 Hours
findings.affected_technology: OpenClaw versions prior to 2026.4.10 (agent platform; MCP transport, gateway control, workspace dotenv handling, ACP session boundary, webhook secret cache)
findings.summary: VulnCheck published a second OpenClaw batch (16 CVEs) on 2026-05-11, on top of the 9-CVE batch from 2026-05-09, bringing cumulative exposure on the pre-2026.4.10 baseline to 25 CVEs in 72 hours.

findings.title: GhostLock Disruption Tool — Windows CreateFileW Exclusive-Access Abuse as Data-Distraction Primitive
findings.affected_technology: Windows (CreateFileW kernel32 API, SMB share access semantics)
findings.summary: Israel Aerospace Industries researcher Kim Dvash published GhostLock — a PoC that opens files with CreateFileW dwShareMode=0 across local and SMB shares to deny access without encrypting or deleting data, evading standard ransomware detection.
findings.first_seen_at: bleepingcomputer.com — New GhostLock tool abuses Windows API to block file access
